clue.text: Shattered Bosnia team can't stand

indicators.note: something shattered is broken to pieces, so the letters of the two words are reassembled

explanation.surface: A demoralised Bosnian football side cannot bear something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' looks like a description of the exhausted team, but it rearranges the ten letters of BOSNIA TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is to be unable to stand it; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Yes, a foreign gamble generates complaint

parts.note: ja is German for yes; 'foreign' applies to this word as well
un is the French for a
to dice is to gamble, as with dice games

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to a bet abroad, and the gamble leads to grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' serves both 'Yes' (German JA) and 'a' (French UN).
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, and this liver disorder yellowing the skin is one.

clue.text: Philby stopped one of his sort revealing much

indicators.note: to stop something up is to plug it, so one name sits inside the other word

parts.note: Philby was a spy, so one of his kind is a spy
Kim Philby was the British double agent who spied for the Soviets

explanation.surface: The notorious traitor halted a fellow agent who was giving too much away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing much' suggests disclosing secrets, apt for a spy, but here it describes scanty clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing covers little and so shows plenty of the body, the sense of an outfit revealing much.

clue.text: No loose end in long story

indicators.note: 'No' says the letter that follows is to be absent from the other word

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn for it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A rambling tale that ties up every loose end.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'loose' is E; YEARN without it leaves the answer. 'long story' reads as one phrase but splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a tale, especially a long, rambling or tall one, so it is a kind of story.

clue.text: Old prince worried voters

parts.note: the Electors were the princes of the Holy Roman Empire who chose its emperor
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: An aged prince grew anxious about his voters.
explanation.walkthrough: An Elector was a historical German prince, such as the Elector of Hanover; 'worried' gives ATE through the sense of something eating at you.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote in an election.

clue.text: Follow boat right in its wake at sea

indicators.note: 'in' puts the single letter within the jumbled letters
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Instructions for a vessel: keep to starboard in its trail out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ITS WAKE, and R goes among those letters. The surface is all seafaring, so 'Follow boat' hardly looks like a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterskier is towed behind a motorboat, so to waterski is literally to follow a boat across the water.

clue.text: Film ghastly chops and scary ending

indicators.note: something ghastly is horribly disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A movie with gruesome hacking and a frightening finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ghastly' rearranges CHOPS together with Y, the last letter of 'scary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1960 horror film with its infamous shower scene; the clue's description fits the movie itself.

clue.text: Insecure Arabs? Some may do this

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Nervous Arab horses might stand up on their hind legs.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabs here are horses; a nervous horse may rise on its hind legs. 'Some' does double duty, picking out the hidden letters and acting as the subject of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that rears lifts its forelegs off the ground, what a skittish horse may do.

clue.text: Need money in small bar at Lord's for crime

indicators.note: 'in' places the need and money inside the cricket term

parts.note: a bail is one of the two small crosspieces on a cricket wicket; Lord's is London's famous cricket ground
a lack is a need or want
M is the abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped person at a cricket-ground bar turns to wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the placing. A bail is one of the little wooden pieces resting on top of the stumps in cricket; 'bar' suggests a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Extorting money by threatening to reveal secrets is a criminal offence.

clue.text: No-frills hellfire preacher's way in church

indicators.note: frills are the edges of a garment, so the name loses its outer letters

parts.note: Ian Paisley, the Northern Irish politician and fire-and-brimstone Free Presbyterian minister

explanation.surface: A fiery evangelist's plain route into his chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley was a Northern Ireland firebrand preacher and politician; strip his name of P and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is the passage between pews, the way people walk through a church.

clue.text: Crew twice reserves Times for islander

indicators.note: to reserve is to keep held, so the repeated word holds the sign
twice means the word is written two times

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

explanation.surface: A newspaper keeps a double crew for a man from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN MAN holds X, the times sign. 'Times' looks like the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is so called, so he is an islander.

clue.text: He squeezes business out of 2000 roubles

indicators.note: out of means without, so the numerals leave the word

parts.note: commerce is business or trade
M is the Roman numeral for 1000, so 2000 is MM
R is the abbreviation for roubles, the Russian currency

explanation.surface: An extortionist who wrings his trade out of two thousand Russian notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes the Roman two thousand; the surface makes it sound like extracting cash from roubles.
explanation.definitionFit: One who coerces applies pressure or force to make others comply, putting the squeeze on them.

clue.text: Top seed Simon's making a racket

parts.note: the top seed in a tournament is number one, written NO 1 with the 1 as I
Sy is a short form of the name Simon; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: The leading tennis player called Simon is noisily complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: NO 1 (with I for one) is the top seed; Sy is a pet form of Simon. 'racket' looks like a tennis bat but means din.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and clamorous describes someone creating a din, which is what a racket is.

clue.text: Poles invested in low quality gem

indicators.note: to invest in is to be put inside, so the poles go within the other words

parts.note: a cow lows, so to low is to moo
tone is a quality, as of sound or character
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish investors put money into a cheap jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: MOO + TONE takes in N and S. 'Poles' suggests people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearly, opalescent feldspar valued as a semi-precious stone, so it is a gem.

clue.text: Mum cooked with onions, left out dressing

parts.note: ma is a word for mother

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter leaves the cooking term

parts.note: lyonnaise is the culinary term for food cooked with onions, as in Lyon

explanation.surface: Mother made a dish with onions but forgot to add the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: LYONNAISE loses L for 'left out'. The surface makes 'left out' sound like an omitted ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick egg-and-oil emulsion is used as a salad dressing.

clue.text: Course records by Woods playing with disheartened men

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: playing suggests moving about freely, so the letters are rearranged
losing its heart, the word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A golf course where Tiger Woods plays alongside dejected opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' and 'Woods' suggest golf, but this is a racecourse. 'disheartened' drops the centre of 'men' and 'playing' shuffles the result with the golfer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is the racecourse that stages the Derby, so it is a course.

clue.text: Film society magazine is no more

parts.note: The Lady is a long-running British weekly magazine for genteel society
something that vanishes disappears and is gone

explanation.surface: A movie about a glossy society magazine folding.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady is a British weekly magazine known for its classified ads for nannies and housekeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1938 thriller set on a train, so it names a film.

clue.text: Local drunk had food to share out

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and unsteady, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: to eat a meal is to have food, past tense ate

explanation.surface: A tipsy regular from the pub ate and then divided up the spoils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges LOCAL; 'Local' suggests a pub regular, since a British local is a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot or distribute portions among people is to share them out.

clue.text: Dreadful writer goes in for rich novel

indicators.note: goes in says the writer's letter is placed among the others
novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A poor author tries writing a novel to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges FOR RICH and I goes in. 'novel' looks like a book the writer produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horrific is appalling or terrible, a synonym for dreadful.

clue.text: Show odd features of 20 during late get-together?

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another

parts.note: a seance is a gathering to contact the late, that is the dead

indicators.note: the odd features are the first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: the answer to 20 down, a cellphone

explanation.surface: Odd aspects of a phone are revealed at a late-night party.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points to the answer at 20 down; 'during' places its odd letters in the gathering. 'late' means dead, not after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A semblance is an outward show or appearance, as in a semblance of order.

clue.text: Agent imports hybrid phone

indicators.note: to import is to bring something in, so the word goes inside

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
bi- means two, as in a hybrid of two kinds

explanation.surface: A spy smuggles in a dual-purpose handset.
explanation.walkthrough: MOLE takes in BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is the usual British name for a cellphone.

clue.text: Wags here are occupying monarch

indicators.note: to occupy is to be inside, so the word sits within the abbreviation

parts.note: HM is short for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: Footballers' wives and girlfriends are entertaining the king.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs is British tabloid shorthand for footballers' wives and girlfriends; 'here' makes the definition the place where such partners are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the quarters housing a ruler's wives and concubines, a place of wives and girlfriends.

clue.text: Woman harnessing King of France's horse

indicators.note: to harness is to hold in, so the woman holds the king

parts.note: hen is slang for a woman, as in hen night
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A woman puts tack on the French king's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is drug slang for the opiate, not the animal the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is a long-standing slang term for the opiate drug, along with smack and H.

clue.text: Book about cricket club on board airline once

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: on board means inside the carrier, so the club is placed within it

parts.note: BEA was British European Airways, absorbed into British Airways in 1974

explanation.surface: A book about a cricket team flying on a defunct airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts the club inside the old airline, British European Airways, which merged into British Airways in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel of the second Mrs de Winter is a famous book.

clue.text: Film Cole Porter piece, sending it up

indicators.note: in a down light, sending up means turning the letters upward, back to front
a piece is a part of the words, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A movie spoofing a song by Cole Porter.
explanation.walkthrough: EPOR spans 'Cole Porter'; 'sending it up' turns it, and the surface makes it sound like a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1948 thriller shot to look like one continuous take is a film.

clue.text: Spinning sensation extremely briefly chasing game at Oval

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: very means extremely
tig is the children's chasing game also called tag
O is oval in shape

explanation.surface: A dizzy feeling after a very quick game at the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: VER (VERY cut short) then TIG and O. The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here it is just a ring-shaped letter; 'chasing' is apt since tig is a chasing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is dizziness in which the surroundings seem to whirl, a spinning sensation.

clue.text: Permit to enter Sweden through borders

indicators.note: the outer word borders the inner letter on both sides

parts.note: via means through, by way of
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A pass to get into Sweden by crossing its frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: VIA borders S.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement allowing its holder entry into a foreign country.

clue.text: Test bed with someone in it?

indicators.note: in it says the person is placed inside the bed

parts.note: a plot is a garden bed
I is the Roman numeral one, here someone

explanation.surface: Trying out a mattress by having a person lie in it.
explanation.walkthrough: PLOT holds I. 'bed' suggests furniture but is a garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial run, as in a pilot scheme or pilot episode.

clue.text: South American still at home harbouring old doubt

parts.note: a still is a photograph, a pic

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter, so one word holds the other

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A Latin American stays home with a lingering misgiving.
explanation.walkthrough: S, US and PIC, then IN holding O. 'still' looks like an adverb but is a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a feeling that something may be wrong, a sense of mistrust or doubt.
